name: Eton-Mengisa
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Van de Velde, Mark (2008), A Grammar of Eton, Mouton de Gruyter (Mouton Grammar Library 46) — phonology chapter; paywalled, not opened

new_statements.quote: Accent in Eton meets Hyman's (to appear) definitional criteria obligatoriness and culminativity, with the minor complication, perhaps, that reduplicated stems have two accentuated syllables (see III:2.3 for examples of reduplication). Every first and only the first syllable of a prosodic stem is accentuated. A prosodic stem is identical to a morphological stem, except if the latter begins in a vowel and if it is preceded by a C-prefix. In that case, the prefix consonant also belongs to the prosodic stem. [...] The phonetic correlate of accent in Eton is consonant length. All other things being equal, consonants in the onset of an accentuated syllable (C1-position) are longer than consonants elsewhere.
new_statements.citation: Van de Velde, Mark L.O. (2006). A Description of Eton: Phonology, morphology, basic syntax and lexicon. PhD thesis, Katholieke Universiteit Leuven. Chapter 2 (Phonology), §3.1 'Accent', pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 38-39).
new_statements.locator: Ch. 2, §3.1 Accent, pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 38-39); see also §3 intro p. 22, §1.2 p. 4, and §3.1 continuation pp. 24-26. Corroborated in French in Van de Velde & Essele Essele 2022, Dictionnaire éton-français, §8.2 p. 19 (PDF p. 28), file.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Eton is a two-tone language that additionally has an obligatory, culminative, demarcative word accent fixed on the first syllable of the (prosodic) stem, i.e. stem-initially rather than word-initially, since noun-class and other prefixes precede the stem and are unaccented. The accent is realised not by vowel length, pitch or intensity but by lengthening of the stem-initial (onset) consonant (roughly twice the duration of other consonants), with associated non-lenition of C1 and phonotactic restriction of half the consonant inventory to C1; unaccented vowels may be secondarily reduced. The French-language dictionary sketch (2022, p. 19) states the same rule: 'l'accent de mot... tombe toujours sur la première syllabe des thèmes'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; the only multi-accent case is reduplicated stems, which carry two accented syllables (one per stem copy). Prefix consonants outside the prosodic stem are intermediate in length but classed as unaccented.
new_statements.exceptions: Reduplicated stems have two accentuated syllables (culminativity 'minor complication'); prefix consonants incorporated into a prosodic stem before vowel-initial stems are accented (and measured even longer); vowel reduction of unaccented syllables is only a secondary, non-exceptionless correlate; author notes descriptions of closely related Ewondo and Mangisa never recognised the accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level demarcative accent defined on the prosodic stem (morphological stem plus any C-prefix before a vowel-initial stem); prefixes are unaccented; measured in spontaneous speech and in nonsense words in isolation and in clauses. Eton is also a two-tone (H/L) language; accent and tone coexist (p. 4: 'Eton has both tone and demarcative word accent'). Phrase-level C-emphasis on focused words is discussed in the 2016 slides.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Eton proper (ìtón, Bantu A71) as spoken in the Lékié department north of Yaoundé; the author distinguishes Northern and Southern Eton (super)dialects but treats accent as pan-Eton. The Glottolog unit eton1253 'Eton-Mengisa' also covers Mengisa (njɔwi, Beti cluster), which is not described in any opened source; Van de Velde 2006: 26 remarks that existing descriptions of Ewondo and Mangisa did not recognise the accent, so the Mengisa side is unverified. The 2022 dictionary sketch is based on the Obala-area speech of the Eton language committee.

sources.note: Ch. 2 §3.1 'Accent' pp. 22-26: Eton has tone and demarcative word accent; every first and only the first syllable of the prosodic stem is accentuated (obligatory, culminative; reduplicated stems have two accented syllables); the phonetic correlate is consonant length (C1 consonants >2x longer), not vowel length, pitch or intensity; prefixes are unaccented; also p. 4 'Eton has both tone and demarcative word accent.'

sources.note: Esquisse grammaticale §8.2, p. 19 (PDF p. 28): 'l'accent de mot, qui en éton tombe toujours sur la première syllabe des thèmes. Cet accent se fait sentir principalement dans la consonne initiale de la syllabe accentuée, qui peut être allongée... Notez que la première syllabe du thème n'est généralement pas la première syllabe du mot.' §8.3 p. 21: two tones, H and L, lexically distinctive.

sources.citation: Van de Velde, Mark & Dmitry Idiatov (2016). Stem-initial accent and C-emphasis prosody in north-western Bantu. Slides, ACAL 47, Berkeley, 26 Mar 2016 (HAL halshs-01481521); same title at Bantu 6, Helsinki 2016 (HAL halshs-01481547).
sources.note: Slide 2: in Eton stem-initial accent is manifested phonotactically (half the consonant phonemes restricted to C1), phonetically (C1 longer), phonologically (C1 not lenited) and tonologically (only accented syllables host two underlying tones); instrumental questionnaire data (9 Eton speakers) confirm C-lengthening as the major correlate; C-emphasis also marks focus.
